clusters.title: Public repository ships no LICENSE while README claims it is private
clusters.description: No LICENSE, COPYING or NOTICE file is tracked. An unauthenticated git ls-remote against origin returned refs/heads/main, refs/heads/ToF and refs/heads/ver1, so the repository is publicly readable. README.md says the licence is still missing and that the repository is private, which is false. Under default copyright a public repository with no licence grants third parties no right to use, modify or redistribute the 13,282 code lines.
clusters.evidence: README.md:114-116 says the repository licence is still missing and currently a private repository, so of no concern. `git ls-remote --heads origin` without supplying credentials returned refs/heads/main, refs/heads/ToF and refs/heads/ver1. `git ls-files` contains no LICENSE, COPYING or NOTICE path.
clusters.recommendation: Add an Apache-2.0 LICENSE and a NOTICE covering sherpa-onnx and other third-party components, correct the README claim, and record an explicit written decision about the CC BY-NC-ND model weights.

instances.title: Legacy WebRTC demo is unauthenticated and proxies the operator Gemini key
instances.description: app.main:app exposes WebRTC signalling, image, audio and ZIP retrieval and Gemini-backed analysis with no authentication, no rate limiting, one global session, and no explicit size cap on the SDP payload. create_offer holds session_lock while waiting up to 15 seconds for ICE gathering, so one request stalls every other offer. The only control is a README sentence telling operators not to expose it, while the same repository ships a full requirements.txt that makes running the demo easy.
instances.evidence: app/main.py:65 declares `@app.post('/api/webrtc/offer')` with no auth dependency; app/main.py:152-183 calls vision.analyze with the server-side GEMINI_API_KEY; app/main.py:144-203 returns the active session image, audio and ZIP; app/main.py:75-82 holds session_lock across setRemoteDescription and up to 15 seconds of ICE gathering; README.md:16 only warns not to put app.main:app on the Internet.
instances.impact: If bound to 0.0.0.0 or tunnelled like the mobile API already is, any stranger can burn the operator paid Gemini quota, read the active user photo, audio, transcript and export bundle, and exhaust CPU or file descriptors with unthrottled offers.
instances.recommendation: Remove the demo from the deployable image and public requirements, or add Bearer authentication, loopback binding at the socket level, per-IP rate limiting and a body cap; separate demo dependencies from the mobile runtime.

instances.title: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 Zipformer weights are baked into the distributable container image
instances.description: The model stage downloads hynt/Zipformer-30M-RNNT-Streaming-6000h into /opt/zipformer and the runtime stage copies it in, so every built image redistributes the weights. README.md states the weights are CC BY-NC-ND 4.0; NC forbids commercial use, ND forbids distributing modified or derivative weights including quantisation and fine-tuning needed for latency work, and attribution terms are not packaged as a NOTICE.
instances.evidence: Dockerfile:7 runs `python scripts/download_model.py --model-dir /opt/zipformer`; Dockerfile:24 copies `/opt/zipformer` into the runtime image; model_config.json:2 pins `hynt/Zipformer-30M-RNNT-Streaming-6000h`; README.md:109 states CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 and README.md:112 warns not to relicense the weights.
instances.impact: A funded or paid pilot, or pushing the image to any registry, is a licence violation; model optimisation is foreclosed because a quantised or fine-tuned derivative cannot be distributed.
instances.recommendation: Keep weights out of the image and download or mount them at runtime under the operator own licence acceptance; package attribution and NOTICE material; evaluate a permissively licensed Vietnamese ASR model for any commercial path.

instances.title: Gemini client honours proxy environment variables and can send the API key through an unintended proxy
instances.description: GeminiVisionProvider builds an httpx.AsyncClient without trust_env=False, so httpx honours HTTPS_PROXY, ALL_PROXY, SSL_CERT_FILE and related environment variables. The Gemini API key is sent in the x-goog-api-key header. The research fetcher deliberately sets trust_env=False in two places, so the egress policy is inconsistent; a compromised or misconfigured proxy environment can route the key, image and transcript through an unintended intermediary.
instances.evidence: app/vision.py:221 creates `httpx.AsyncClient(timeout=self._timeout, transport=self._transport)` without trust_env=False; app/vision.py:224 sends `headers={'x-goog-api-key': self._api_key}`; app/guidance_search.py:159 and app/guidance_search.py:230 explicitly set trust_env=False.
instances.impact: A server-side environment compromise or platform misconfiguration can expose the Gemini key and user media to a proxy, and egress becomes non-deterministic across deployments.
instances.recommendation: Pass trust_env=False to the Gemini client, document the required egress path, and add a regression test with proxy environment variables set; consider a dedicated egress client or allowlist.

instances.title: Admission control is process-local and breaks when the service scales beyond one worker
instances.description: WorkGate is an in-memory dict of leases with capacity 2 and one identity per token. The Docker image runs uvicorn with --workers 1 and the Cloud Run reference uses --max-instances 1; the documentation itself notes that multiple replicas need shared admission. Any horizontal scale-out, or an accidental --workers 2, gives each process its own gate, so the documented one-active-per-token and two-global-AI-job limits no longer hold.
instances.evidence: app/mobile_security.py:79-88 stores leases in a local dict and checks `len(self._leases) >= self.capacity or identity in self._leases`; Dockerfile:30 runs `--workers 1`; docs/ANDROID_SETUP.md:88 says multiple replicas need shared admission.
instances.impact: Under scale-out one token can run multiple concurrent AI jobs, and the operator can exceed the intended Gemini concurrency and cost envelope; CPU and STT contention and quota exhaustion become possible.
instances.recommendation: Move admission to a shared atomic store such as Redis with a per-token lease and a global semaphore, or enforce a single instance and fail startup when workers exceed one; add a regression test with two app instances sharing one gate.

instances.title: Static bearer tokens have no expiry, rotation or per-token request quota
instances.description: Trial tokens are 256-bit random values, but the server stores only SHA-256 digests with no issued_at, expiry, label or usage counter. Revocation requires editing TRIAL_TOKEN_HASHES and restarting the process. There is no per-token request-rate or spend cap; the gate only limits concurrent jobs. A leaked token therefore remains valid indefinitely and can serially consume Gemini quota until an operator notices and restarts.
instances.evidence: app/mobile_security.py:19-27 stores only a tuple of 64-hex digests; app/mobile_security.py:37-46 hashes the presented token and compares; docs/ANDROID_SETUP.md:28-35 describes revocation by deleting the hash and restarting; app/mobile_security.py:76-88 limits concurrency rather than request rate.
instances.impact: Lost or stolen tester tokens grant indefinite access; there is no per-user audit trail or spend attribution; incident response requires a full process restart.
instances.recommendation: Store token metadata including label, issued_at, expires_at, last_used and request_count; enforce expiry and a per-token rate or spend budget; support revocation without restart through a Redis denylist; log a token identifier, never the token.

instances.title: Missing Root Repository License
instances.description: Repository documentation acknowledges the license is missing; creates legal ambiguity for third-party contributors and pilot testers.
instances.evidence: README explicitly references absent license terms and prospective licensing.
instances.recommendation: Adopt standard open-source license file (MIT or Apache 2.0).

instances.title: Root README Architectural Disconnect and Conflicting Entry Points
instances.description: The root README instructs users to launch a local desktop WebRTC Chrome demo (app.main:app) while the production mobile API is app.mobile_api:app. It also showcases speculative hardware (VL53L9CX ToF LiDAR) without codebase integration, and contains explicit author confusion notes regarding versions and tokens.
instances.evidence: README lines 16, 128: 'I\'m not sure why we need a Gemini token. Or what the v0.2.1 version of the Android app did. Or v0.3 or v0.4. You might try it out.'
instances.impact: Creates severe cognitive friction, onboarding failure, and uncertainty for reviewers and engineers attempting to operate the system.
instances.recommendation: Restructure root README with a unified architectural diagram clearly separating the Android client, the FastAPI Docker container, the local Zipformer STT engine, and the Gemini 3.8 Flash cloud API.

instances.title: Unauthenticated legacy WebRTC demo retains session seizure and media export endpoints
instances.description: app.main defines a complete local demo with no authentication on any route. POST /api/webrtc/offer accepts an arbitrary SDP, creates or replaces the single global active_session, and returns its UUID. DELETE /api/sessions/{id}, GET /api/sessions/{id}/turns/{turn_id}/image, GET .../audio, and GET .../export then expose captured camera frames, microphone WAV, and a ZIP bundle to any caller that has the session UUID. The Dockerfile copies the whole app/ directory, so main.py and session.py ship in the image even though the production CMD starts app.mobile_api:app. The production requirements-mobile.txt omits aiortc, so the demo is not runnable in the default container, but it is runnable on a host that installs requirements.txt, which the root README instructs users to do. Because only one demo session may exist, an unauthenticated peer can also hold the slot and force 409 responses for the legitimate operator.
instances.impact: If the demo is exposed on a LAN, a tunnel, or a misconfigured host, an unauthenticated network peer can occupy the only session, read the blind user's camera snapshots and microphone recording, download the turn ZIP, and terminate sessions. This is sensitive media and a trivial denial of service. The default container command does not expose these routes, so the finding is conditional on operator behavior rather than exploitable in the shipped CMD.
instances.recommendation: Move the demo into a separate package or directory that is excluded from the runtime image, or mount its routes only when an explicit DEMO_MODE flag is set and require the same bearer authentication. Remove the media/export routes from any network-reachable build, or gate them behind an authenticated local operator. Add a negative test asserting that app.mobile_api exposes no /api/webrtc or /api/sessions routes, and make the README state unambiguously that the demo is not part of the production service.

instances.title: Trial tokens never expire and revocation requires an environment edit plus restart
instances.description: TrialTokens stores up to ten SHA-256 digests parsed from TRIAL_TOKEN_HASHES. The digests have no issuance time, expiry, owner label, last-used timestamp, or revoked flag. Identification is a constant-time comparison loop over the current tuple, which is good, but the only revocation path is to edit the environment and restart the process. The architecture document states this explicitly. Tokens are also shared secrets rather than per-person credentials, so a leaked token cannot be attributed or selectively expired without restarting the service for everyone.
instances.impact: A token copied from a test device, chat message, or screen recording remains valid indefinitely. There is no way to expire a single pilot participant, no audit of which token made a request, and no short-lived credential to limit blast radius. A compromised token also consumes the same shared concurrency and Gemini budget as a legitimate user.
instances.recommendation: Replace the environment tuple with a small token table (PostgreSQL or Redis) containing token_hash, owner_label, issued_at, expires_at, revoked_at, and last_used_at. Issue short-lived tokens with a refresh path or a pilot expiry date. Add an admin-only revoke operation that takes effect on the next request, and log the owner label with each request code. Keep the current fail-closed parsing and constant-time comparison.

instances.title: No per-token rate limit; one valid token can monopolize shared capacity and buffer v3 bodies
instances.description: WorkGate enforces a global capacity of two and one lease per token identity, but it has no rate, quota, or fairness window. A token can issue sequential requests forever and hold a slot for the duration of ASR plus Gemini, so two tokens can starve every other pilot user. The v2 middleware acquires the lease before reading the body, which is good, but the v3 GuidanceAdmissionMiddleware authenticates and then buffers up to MAX_BODY_BYTES (about 2 MiB) before GuidanceService.submit acquires a WorkGate lease. A valid token can therefore open many concurrent v3 uploads and create memory pressure before admission control applies. Unauthenticated health checks and 401 attempts are also unbounded, although they are cheap.
instances.evidence:
app/mobile_security.py:
  def acquire(self, identity: str) -> WorkLease | None:
      if len(self._leases) >= self.capacity or identity in self._leases:
          return None
      ...

  lease = self.gate.acquire(identity)
  if lease is None:
      await self._error(scope, receive, send, 429, "Đang xử lý lượt khác. Hãy thử lại sau.")

app/guidance_api.py:
  # authenticates, then reads the whole body into memory
  while True:
      message = await receive()
      total += len(message.get("body", b""))
      if total > MAX_BODY_BYTES: ...
  await self.app(scope, replay, send)

app/guidance.py (inside submit, after the body has already been parsed):
  lease = self.gate.acquire(owner)
instances.impact: A single trial participant can deny service to the other participant and burn Gemini quota with a loop of valid requests. A malicious or buggy client can also cause avoidable memory and CPU pressure by opening many v3 uploads. The impact is bounded by authentication and the two-slot gate, but the control is concurrency-only, not abuse-resistant.
instances.recommendation: Add a token-bucket or sliding-window limiter keyed by token identity and, at the ingress, by client IP (for example 6 requests per minute and a daily cap per trial token), returning 429 with Retry-After. Apply the same admission lease before reading v3 bodies, or add a separate bounded upload gate. Add alerting on 429/401 rates and on per-token Gemini spend. If the pilot grows beyond one process, move admission and quotas to a shared Redis-backed gate rather than multiplying the in-process capacity.

instances.title: Admin localhost guard trusts the Host header and socket peer, so a local proxy can expose approval actions
instances.description: The knowledge-review console decides whether a request is local by parsing the Host header and comparing request.client.host with a loopback set. Both values are weak authorization signals. If the console is placed behind a reverse proxy or relay that runs on the same host, request.client.host is 127.0.0.1 for every remote request, and the Host header can be forged to localhost. The launch script binds the app to 127.0.0.1, which blocks direct remote connections, but the guard is the only defense if that binding is changed or a local proxy is added. Login also has no throttling; the admin secret is required to be at least 24 characters, which makes brute force impractical but not impossible if the secret is weak or reused.
instances.evidence:
app/guidance_admin.py: host = request.headers.get("host", "").lower() hostname = urlsplit("http://" + host).hostname client = request.client.host if request.client else "" if hostname not in {"127.0.0.1", "localhost", "::1"} or client not in {"127.0.0.1", "::1", "testclient"}: return _page("

Trang duyệt chỉ mở trên máy chủ localhost.

", 403) scripts/run_guidance_admin.sh: exec .venv/bin/python -m uvicorn app.guidance_admin:app --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8081 ...
instances.impact: Knowledge profiles approved through this console become guidance used by blind users. If the console is accidentally proxied, a remote party could approve, suspend, or edit draft profiles, undermining the human review gate. The loopback bind substantially reduces the likelihood, hence probable rather than verified.
instances.recommendation: Keep the loopback bind and document it as an invariant. Do not use Host or socket peer as the primary authorization decision; require the admin secret on every state-changing request (or an HMAC-signed request), not only at login. Add login throttling and an idle timeout. If TLS termination is ever added, set the cookie Secure flag and verify the exact configured origin rather than a derived base URL. Consider binding to a Unix socket or a dedicated loopback port with firewall rules.

instances.title: No repository license while model weights are CC BY-NC-ND 4.0; visibility claims are contradictory
instances.description: The repository has no LICENSE, COPYING, or NOTICE file at its root. The README explicitly says the repository license is still missing and that the project is currently private. At the same time, the 0.4.0 release document links a public GitHub archive path for the source. The bundled Zipformer weights are identified as CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, which prohibits commercial use and distribution of derivatives; the sherpa-onnx runtime is Apache-2.0. Without a root license, default copyright applies to the code and no permission is granted to copy, modify, or distribute it, even for a pilot. The contradiction between private and public distribution statements makes the actual confidentiality and licensing posture unclear.
instances.evidence:
README.md:

  It is still missing, follow the guidance above from other repositories. Currently a private
  repository, so of no concern.

README.md:
  Model: hynt/Zipformer-30M-RNNT-Streaming-6000h; license weights theo model card: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0.
  STT runtime: sherpa-onnx; license code runtime: Apache-2.0.

docs/RELEASE_040.md:
  [Tải source hiện tại trên GitHub](https://github.com/thanh1912-ut/.../archive/refs/heads/main.zip)
instances.impact: A commercial pilot or public distribution has no code license and cannot rely on the NC-ND model weights. Contributors and testers have no clear grant. If the repository is in fact public, the README's privacy statement is inaccurate and may mislead users about the exposure of source, documentation, and release links. If it is private, the public archive link is stale or broken. Either way, legal and onboarding risk is material.
instances.recommendation: Add a root LICENSE (for example Apache-2.0 or MIT for the code) plus a NOTICE that separately records the Zipformer CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 terms, the sherpa-onnx Apache-2.0 terms, and any dataset terms. Add SPDX headers to source files. State repository visibility accurately in the README and release notes, and remove public archive links if the project is private. If commercial use is intended, replace the NC-ND model or obtain explicit permission; do not assume the runtime license covers the weights.

instances.title: Client accepts any HTTPS backend and sends the trial token plus camera and audio data to it
instances.description: normalizeBaseUrl validates only that the value parses as an HTTPS URL without embedded credentials, query, or fragment. Any host is accepted. api.ts then sends Authorization: Bearer <trialToken> and a multipart body containing a JPEG and audio or transcript to that host. There is no allowlist, pinned certificate, signed remote configuration, or host-change confirmation. Settings are user-editable, and the target user may rely on spoken setup or assistance from another person, which makes a social-engineering attack ("enter this server address") plausible.
instances.impact: A user who is tricked into entering an attacker-controlled HTTPS endpoint will transmit a valid trial token and sensitive camera/audio content. The attacker can then reuse the token against the real service and retain the media. The client's otherwise careful error handling and SecureStore storage do not mitigate this, because the destination itself is untrusted.
instances.recommendation: For the pilot, pin the expected backend host or a signed allowlist in the app configuration, and require an explicit spoken and visual confirmation when the host changes. Consider certificate pinning or app attestation for the production build. If self-hosted servers must remain supported, separate that build flavor and add a prominent host-verification step. Never re-send the token automatically after a host change.

instances.description: The target tracks no LICENSE, COPYING or NOTICE file, yet the remote is publicly readable: an unauthenticated git ls-remote against origin returned refs/heads/main, refs/heads/ToF and refs/heads/ver1. instances.title: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 Zipformer weights are baked into the distributable container image
instances.description: The first build stage downloads the Hugging Face weights into /opt/zipformer and the runtime stage copies them in, so every built image redistributes CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 licensed weights inside a new artifact. ND forbids distributing derived or repackaged versions, which also rules out the quantisation or fine-tuning needed to reach the project's own latency target, and NC forbids commercial use.

instances.title: Legacy demo application is fully unauthenticated and proxies the operator's paid Gemini key
instances.description: app.main:app exposes WebRTC signalling, image and audio retrieval, ZIP export and Gemini-backed analysis with no authentication, no rate limiting and a single global session. The only control preventing internet exposure is one sentence in the README, while the same codebase already demonstrates the correct control in the admin app, which enforces loopback host and client addresses in middleware.
instances.evidence: app/main.py:65 declares the offer endpoint with no auth dependency; app/main.py:152-183 calls vision.analyze using the server-side GEMINI_API_KEY; app/main.py:194-203 returns a ZIP of the user's photo, audio and transcript. README.md:16 only says not to put app.main:app on the Internet. Contrast app/guidance_admin.py:75-83 which enforces loopback programmatically.
instances.impact: If bound to a non-loopback interface or tunnelled the way the mobile API already is, any stranger can burn the operator's Gemini quota, read the active session's photo, audio and export bundle, and exhaust CPU through unthrottled offers that each run a 15-second ICE-gathering loop.
instances.recommendation: Apply the guidance_admin loopback middleware to app.main, or require a bearer token, and refuse to bind a non-loopback host unless an explicit opt-in environment variable is set.

instances.title: One in-process two-slot gate is shared by the v2 and v3 APIs and cannot scale horizontally
instances.description: WorkGate is a plain dictionary on the event loop, instantiated once and handed to both the mobile admission middleware and the guidance service. Guidance operations are long-lived (a Gemini call, optionally a Brave search and up to three document fetches) and compete for the same two slots as photo-question requests. Because the gate is process-local, adding a worker or a replica silently multiplies real capacity and breaks the per-token guarantee.
instances.evidence: app/mobile_api.py:163 gate = WorkGate(capacity=2); app/mobile_api.py:179 install_guidance(application, tokens, gate, ...); app/guidance.py:214 lease = self.gate.acquire(owner); Dockerfile:30 runs --workers 1 with the comment that one process keeps the two-slot and per-token limits global.
instances.impact: A single user running device guidance can starve every other user's analyze and transcribe request with 429 server_busy. The documented pilot ceiling is two concurrent users, and horizontal scaling requires re-implementing admission in Redis first.
instances.recommendation: Move admission to a Redis-backed semaphore (Redis is already a hard runtime dependency), give guidance and v2 separate pools so a long guidance operation cannot block a quick question, and document per-instance capacity.

instances.title: Model weights are trusted on first use; no expected digests are committed
instances.description: The pinned revision is validated as a 40-character hex SHA, but no expected content hash ships in the repository. The digest is computed after download and written to a local manifest, which is then treated as authoritative on subsequent runs. The Docker build performs that first, unverified fetch on the build host.
instances.evidence: scripts/download_model.py:57 computes sha256 of the downloaded file; :64 records it in manifest.json; :39-42 reuses the recorded value as the expected digest only on later runs; Dockerfile:7 executes the download at image build time.
instances.impact: A compromised mirror, a man-in-the-middle on the build host, or a rewritten upstream revision yields weights that are then recorded as trusted and baked into every image. With no CI, nothing would ever detect it, and the model directly shapes what blind users are told about their surroundings.
instances.recommendation: Commit the expected SHA-256 of all four model files in model_config.json and fail the download on mismatch, so integrity does not depend on the machine that happened to fetch first.

instances.title: Pilot traffic is routed through ephemeral Cloudflare quick tunnels to a personal Mac
instances.description: The publicly distributed APK is instructed to point at a trycloudflare hostname that terminates on a developer laptop running uvicorn, PostgreSQL and Redis, with only port 8080 forwarded. Quick tunnels have no stable identity, no edge authentication and rotate on every restart; four different tunnel URLs appear across the release documentation.
instances.evidence: docs/RELEASE_040.md:10 publishes the tunnel URL and :3 the public APK; docs/GUIDANCE_040.md:45 states the tunnel forwards only 8080; further URLs appear at docs/RELEASE_021.md:3, docs/RELEASE_030.md:3 and docs/INPUT_FIX_013.md:41; docs/IMPLEMENTATION_STATUS.md:42 confirms no independent hosting exists.
instances.impact: Confidentiality and availability of blind users' photos, voice and transcripts depend on one laptop staying awake and one tunnel staying alive. A stale URL baked into a distributed APK silently breaks the pilot, and there is no edge rate limiting or WAF in front of the token-only authentication layer.
instances.recommendation: Deploy the existing container to a real host using the Cloud Run recipe already written in docs/ANDROID_SETUP.md:72-88, front it with a stable authenticated domain, and stop publishing tunnel URLs in release notes.

instances.title: Guidance startup swallows every exception without logging
instances.description: Redis, PostgreSQL and Gemini-key failures all collapse into the same silent ready=False. The entire app package contains only five log statements and none of them is in this path, so the server records no reason for the outage.
instances.evidence: app/guidance.py:113-115 catches Exception and sets self.ready = False with the comment that guidance can be unavailable without taking the legacy v2 service down. Compare app/asr.py:62 which does call log.exception on model-load failure.
instances.impact: An operator sees guidance_ready:false in the health payload with no server-side clue which of three dependencies failed, lengthening diagnosis on a laptop-hosted pilot where the operator is also the developer.
instances.recommendation: Call log.exception with the failing dependency name (never the DSN or key) and surface a coarse reason code in the authenticated health response.

instances.title: Admin login has no throttling and all review actions are attributed to one literal identity
instances.description: The single shared admin token can be guessed without limit; there is no attempt counter, backoff or lockout. Every edit, approval and suspension is then recorded against the constant string local-admin, so the audit trail cannot identify who approved knowledge that will be spoken aloud to blind users. Mitigations are real but orthogonal: loopback host and client checks, a 24-character minimum secret, origin validation and HMAC-signed two-hour cookies.
instances.evidence: app/guidance_admin.py:125 compares the secret with no attempt accounting; :175, :212 and :221 all pass the literal reviewer string local-admin; mitigations at :75-89 and :39-48.
instances.impact: Any local process, or a malicious page loaded in a browser on the same machine, can attempt unlimited token guesses, and approved device-guidance profiles carry no accountable approver identity.
instances.recommendation: Add a per-cookie and per-client attempt counter with exponential backoff, and replace the literal reviewer with an authenticated operator name so guidance_reviews is a genuine audit log.

instances.title: Unauthenticated health endpoint discloses internal subsystem readiness
instances.description: The admission middleware guards only POST to the two v2 paths, so the health route answers unauthenticated callers with a per-subsystem breakdown of what is configured and what is down, with no rate limit.
instances.evidence: app/mobile_security.py:16 MOBILE_PATHS contains only /api/v2/analyze and /api/v2/transcribe; app/mobile_api.py:197-199 returns asr_ready, vision_ready, auth_ready, guidance_ready and research_ready.
instances.impact: An unauthenticated observer can fingerprint the deployment and time attacks against a recovering service, and can poll the endpoint freely on a two-slot server.
instances.recommendation: Return a single boolean to unauthenticated callers and expose the detailed breakdown only to requests carrying a valid trial token.

instances.title: Volume-key freshness window compares a wall-clock timestamp against a monotonic event time
instances.description: The native module emits System.currentTimeMillis while the Kotlin policy reasons in Android eventTime, and the JavaScript layer rejects events older than 1500 milliseconds. These are different clock domains, so an NTP step or a manual clock change during a session can invalidate legitimate presses or admit stale ones.
instances.evidence: MatKinhControlsModule.kt emits System.currentTimeMillis(); VolumeKeyPolicy.kt operates on eventTime; mobile/src/hooks/useHardwareControls.ts:47 applies the 1500 ms window; mobile/modules/mat-kinh-controls/index.ts:6 acknowledges the window exists.
instances.impact: For a user whose only reliable input is two volume keys, dropped presses present as an unresponsive app with no spoken error, which is indistinguishable from a crash.
instances.recommendation: Emit SystemClock.uptimeMillis() from the native module and compare against the same monotonic domain in JavaScript.

instances.title: Trial token is duplicated into a second SecureStore journal and replayed after settings change
instances.description: The recovery journal stores the API base URL, trial token and client request ID under a second SecureStore key so a pending task can be cancelled after a crash, reusing the old credential even after the user has rotated settings. The design is defensible and bounded by a 31-minute TTL and by errors that cannot block new credentials, but it doubles the number of places a live token rests.
instances.evidence: mobile/src/services/deviceRecovery.ts:33 writes the journal; :52-58 replays the stored token and URL to DELETE the pending task; :48 applies the TTL; :59-61 ensures failures cannot block new credentials; storage uses WHEN_UNLOCKED_THIS_DEVICE_ONLY at mobile/src/hooks/useSettings.ts:39.
instances.impact: A keystore compromise, or a pilot device handed to the next user without a wipe, exposes a valid token plus the server URL for up to 31 minutes after credential rotation.
instances.recommendation: Clear the recovery journal on explicit logout and token rotation, and bind each journal entry to the hash of the token that created it.

clusters.title: Denial-of-Service Risk via Unthrottled Public Endpoints
clusters.description: While WorkGate caps active inference to 2 slots, public endpoints (/api/health, /api/webrtc/offer) lack IP-based rate limiting, allowing connection flooding.
clusters.evidence: FastAPI routers declare no request throttling or IP limiters on exposed /health or /api/webrtc/offer endpoints.
clusters.recommendation: Wrap FastAPI with slowapi or enforce rate limits at ingress proxy.

instances.title: Admission lease has no timeout, so a wedged ONNX call permanently consumes global capacity
instances.description: A lease is released only by the bound worker's done-callback, and there is no deadline, TTL or reaper. Decoding runs in asyncio.to_thread under a process-wide threading.Lock and cannot be preempted; the cooperative stop flag is only checked between decoded frames. Deferred cancellation is deliberate and tested, but no test covers a worker that never returns.
instances.evidence: app/mobile_security.py:68-73 release() sets stop and defers gate release to _worker_finished; app/asr.py:76 and app/asr.py:83 hold _inference_lock across decoding; app/mobile_pipeline.py:92 and :101 poll lease.stop only between frames; tests/test_mobile_api.py:337 and tests/test_mobile_pipeline.py:153 assert the slot is held until the CPU work finishes.
instances.impact: One wedged decode removes half of the two global slots permanently; two wedges are a total outage with no self-healing short of restarting the single uvicorn worker. For a mobility aid, a silent permanent 429 is a safety-relevant failure.
instances.recommendation: Add a lease deadline (for example 90 seconds) with a background reaper that force-releases and logs the event, and expose current slot occupancy through the authenticated health payload.

clusters.title: Model download is trust-on-first-use; no expected SHA-256 is pinned
clusters.description: The download script pins a Hugging Face revision, which is better than tracking main, but it does not verify the downloaded files against a digest that is committed independently. It reads any previous manifest, compares the cache only when the revision matches and an expected digest exists, and otherwise downloads the file, computes its SHA-256, and writes that digest into the new manifest. A compromised upstream account, a malicious model repository, or a first-build interception therefore becomes the trusted baseline. The Docker build performs this download at image build time, so the image inherits the same first-use trust. Python packages are pinned but installed without --require-hashes, so the same first-use concern applies at a lower level.
clusters.recommendation: Commit expected SHA-256 values for all four files in model_config.json and verify each download before use; fail closed on mismatch. Store the expected hashes separately from the generated manifest, sign the manifest if it is distributed, and consider a reproducible download test in CI. Pin pip installs with a hash-checked requirements lock for the image build, and pin the base image by digest.

clusters.title: Upload cleanup depends on a private Starlette attribute inside a finally block
clusters.description: Both multipart helpers reach into an undocumented Starlette internal to close partially spooled uploads, and the admin app assigns another private attribute to inject a buffered body. Starlette is pinned to 0.48.0 but there is no lockfile hash and no CI job, so nothing guards the pin. Because the access sits in a finally block, a rename converts every failed upload into an AttributeError that masks the original exception.
clusters.evidence: app/mobile_api.py:75 iterates parser._files_to_close_on_error; app/guidance_api.py:85 repeats the same pattern; app/guidance_admin.py:97 assigns request._body. tests/test_mobile_api.py:249 and :264 cover the cleanup path against the currently pinned version.
clusters.recommendation: Use getattr with an empty default, or track uploaded files explicitly, and add a CI job that runs the pinned suite on every dependency change.

clusters.title: Dependencies are version-pinned but not hash-locked and there is no CI vulnerability gate
clusters.description: requirements.txt and requirements-mobile.txt pin versions but contain no require-hashes directives; the Docker base images are pinned by tag rather than digest; there is no GitHub Actions workflow, pip-audit, npm audit, osv-scanner, Dependabot, Renovate or SBOM generation. scripts/check.sh only runs tests, compileall, a JavaScript syntax check and TypeScript and Jest. A mutable dependency or base-image tag can enter the build without an automated CVE or provenance gate.
clusters.evidence: requirements.txt:1-56 lists exact versions but no hashes; Dockerfile:1 and Dockerfile:10 use tag-only base images; scripts/check.sh:5-10 runs pytest, compileall, node --check, typecheck and Jest only; the only YAML workflow found is mobile/.eas/workflows/repack-android.yml.
clusters.recommendation: Use a lockfile with hashes via uv or pip-tools, pin image digests, add CI with pip-audit, npm audit and osv-scanner plus an SBOM such as CycloneDX or Syft, and enable automated dependency updates.

clusters.title: Admin localhost check is address-based and can be bypassed by a local reverse proxy or tunnel
clusters.description: The admin app allows requests only when the Host header hostname is 127.0.0.1, localhost or ::1 and request.client.host is loopback or testclient. This is correct for direct localhost use, but it cannot distinguish a local browser from a reverse proxy or tunnel that terminates on loopback and forwards a remote request with a spoofed Host header. The documentation explicitly forbids tunnelling the admin port, but a single operator mistake would expose the admin surface.
clusters.evidence: app/guidance_admin.py:82 checks `if hostname not in {'127.0.0.1','localhost','::1'} or client not in {'127.0.0.1','::1','testclient'}`; docs/GUIDANCE_040.md:45 says not to forward the admin page, PostgreSQL or Redis.
clusters.recommendation: Bind the admin listener to loopback at the socket level or use a Unix socket, reject forwarded headers, and add a deployment check that the admin port is unreachable through the mobile tunnel.

clusters.title: Setup documentation hard-codes a developer's absolute home path
clusters.description: Four setup commands use an absolute path under a named user's home directory. This leaks a local username and machine layout into the repository, and it guarantees that copy-paste onboarding fails on any other machine. It is a documentation and minor information-disclosure issue, not a runtime vulnerability.
clusters.evidence:
docs/ANDROID_SETUP.md contains four `cd` commands that begin with a hard-coded
developer home-directory prefix before the repository folder name, repeated for
the repository root and the mobile directory.
clusters.recommendation: Replace absolute paths with a repository-root variable such as REPO_ROOT="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)" or relative commands. Add a short prerequisite section for Python 3.11, Node, and Android tooling, and test the commands from a clean clone.

reports.target_repo: APEC Mắt Kính Cho Người Khiếm Thị (Smart Glasses for the Blind)
reports.summary: A privacy-conscious, unusually well-threat-modelled assistive Android system for blind Vietnamese users: server-side sherpa-onnx Zipformer STT, Gemini vision behind fail-closed SHA-256 trial tokens, a per-token and two-slot global admission gate, and an Expo/React Native client whose pure TypeScript core enforces HTTPS-only transport, bounded media and screen-reader-aware speech. The engineering of the safety and privacy controls is above pilot grade, but the project is not production-ready: no LICENSE in a public repository, no CI or Python lint/type gate, no dependency hashes, no real-device or blind-user validation, a stale and inconsistent front door, a legacy unauthenticated WebRTC demo with access to the server Gemini key, and a single-process admission model that cannot scale.
key_strengths: Fail-closed mobile authentication and admission: only SHA-256 token digests are stored, malformed configuration disables the service, comparison uses hmac.compare_digest, request bodies are capped before the multipart parser, and a token gets one lease inside a two-slot WorkGate (app/mobile_security.py:19-46, 76-93, 103-177; app/mobile_api.py:162-183).

Privacy-preserving media boundary: ASR runs on the operator server with sherpa-onnx, only discrete JPEG snapshots and short M4A clips are accepted, audio is deleted after transcription, cached media is removed on cancel, expiry and background, and Gemini receives image plus transcript with store=false, never audio (app/mobile_pipeline.py:75-120; mobile/src/core/TurnController.ts:246-266; mobile/src/services/media.ts:20-43; app/vision.py:152-207).

Safety gates treat AI output as an untrusted proposal: the v3 orchestrator owns confirmation, revision, frame deduplication and evidence state; unsafe instructions containing centimetres, multi-press counts, compound actions or a press verb during a locate step are rejected; factory reset, data wipe, purchases and password entry stop before final confirmation; a remote photo cannot prove the target device changed (app/guidance.py:533-535, 540-551, 587-592).

Layered prompt-injection and SSRF defences: system prompts classify transcripts, OCR text, fetched pages and JSON fields as untrusted; the research fetcher resolves DNS once, requires every answer to be global, pins the returned IP while preserving SNI and Host, allowlists official vendor domains, revalidates each redirect, caps bytes and isolates PDF parsing in a subprocess with RLIMIT_CPU and RLIMIT_AS (app/guidance_search.py:93-194, 280-295; app/guidance_vision.py:16-51).

Accessibility is engineered rather than decorative: 56dp minimum controls and an 88dp primary action, allowFontScaling, explicit roles and states, screen-reader announcements, the camera preview excluded from the accessibility tree, reduced-motion-aware transitions, and a Kotlin volume-key policy that yields to TalkBack touch and hover, chords, long presses and repeated events (mobile/src/components/ActionButton.tsx:34-42; mobile/src/components/AppText.tsx:16-20; mobile/src/components/StateTransition.tsx:7-14; mobile/src/screens/HomeScreen.tsx:380; HardwareControlsDispatcher.kt:78-122; VolumeKeyPolicy.kt:20-61).

Unusually deep automated tests for a pilot: 18 Python test modules, 17 Jest suites and 15 Kotlin policy tests assert fail-closed auth, 413-before-parse, private-data-free logs, SSRF rejection, prompt-injection containment, idempotency, revision conflicts, cancellation and lease release, and accessibility labels (tests/test_mobile_api.py:144-220; tests/test_guidance_search.py:56-80; tests/test_guidance.py:91-160; mobile/tests/hardwareControlsNative.test.ts:17-57).
key_weaknesses: No LICENSE in a public repository, and the README says the opposite; CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 Zipformer weights are copied into the Docker image at build time, so the redistributable artifact has unresolved licensing and commercial-use constraints (README.md:109-116; Dockerfile:7-8, 24).

No CI, no Python linter or type checker, no coverage threshold, no dependency hashes or SBOM; checks are a manual shell script, the only tag v0.1.0 points at the 0.4 implementation commit, and git holds only five commits, so the documented 0.1-0.4 history is not reconstructable (scripts/check.sh:1-11; pyproject.toml:1-27; git tag v0.1.0 resolves to 16faf3f).

The product has never met its users: every row of docs/GUIDANCE_ACCEPTANCE_040.md and docs/ANDROID_ACCEPTANCE.md is marked Chưa thử, including 10 remotes, TalkBack, 200 percent font, 20 turns on two phones, and 5 blind users across 6 tasks at 80 percent completion; synthetic fixtures are explicitly not evidence of device support (docs/GUIDANCE_ACCEPTANCE_040.md:3-15; docs/ANDROID_ACCEPTANCE.md:7-28).

The front door mixes two products and is internally inconsistent: it advertises a macOS Chrome WebRTC demo and an unintegrated VL53L9CX LiDAR sensor, defaults to gemini-3.8-flash while the release notes say the demo was moved to gemini-3.1-flash-lite, ships temporary trycloudflare URLs, and includes an author note saying they do not know what v0.2.1 through v0.4 did (README.md:16-31, 118-128; docs/RELEASE_040.md:21, 31).

Two client state machines are maintained but only one runs: HomeScreen hardcodes deviceGuidance true, so the 545-line v2 TurnController and its confirmation and action-menu branches are unreachable in production, while DeviceTaskController exposes compatibility methods that all delegate to start (mobile/src/screens/HomeScreen.tsx:75; mobile/src/hooks/useTurnController.ts:70-72; mobile/src/core/DeviceTaskController.ts:366-371).

Admission and rate control are process-local: WorkGate is an in-memory dict, Docker runs --workers 1, and there is no per-token request-rate or spend cap, so a second worker or replica, or a valid token issuing serial requests, breaks the one-active-per-token and two-global invariant or can drain Gemini quota (app/mobile_security.py:76-93; Dockerfile:30; docs/ANDROID_SETUP.md:88).

The ASR and command layer is brittle for the target user: the v3 backend recognises six exact phrases, the release notes already record Bắt đầu hướng dẫn being transcribed as BÁC ĐẦU HƯỚNG DẪN, and there is no fuzzy repair or explicit I-did-not-catch-you recovery path, which is a safety-critical dead end for a blind user (app/guidance_contract.py:53-64; docs/RELEASE_040.md:27).

security_findings.title: Public repository ships no LICENSE while README claims it is private
security_findings.description: No LICENSE, COPYING or NOTICE file is tracked. An unauthenticated git ls-remote against origin returned refs/heads/main, refs/heads/ToF and refs/heads/ver1, so the repository is publicly readable. README.md says the licence is still missing and that the repository is private, which is false. Under default copyright a public repository with no licence grants third parties no right to use, modify or redistribute the 13,282 code lines.
security_findings.evidence: README.md:114-116 says the repository licence is still missing and currently a private repository, so of no concern. `git ls-remote --heads origin` without supplying credentials returned refs/heads/main, refs/heads/ToF and refs/heads/ver1. `git ls-files` contains no LICENSE, COPYING or NOTICE path.
security_findings.impact: APEC partners, pilot sites, reviewers, contributors and forkers have no legal grant to use the code. The Apache-2.0 sherpa-onnx runtime also requires licence and NOTICE retention that the repository does not provide.
security_findings.recommendation: Add an Apache-2.0 LICENSE and a NOTICE covering sherpa-onnx and other third-party components, correct the README claim, and record an explicit written decision about the CC BY-NC-ND model weights.

security_findings.title: Legacy WebRTC demo is unauthenticated and proxies the operator Gemini key
security_findings.description: app.main:app exposes WebRTC signalling, image, audio and ZIP retrieval and Gemini-backed analysis with no authentication, no rate limiting, one global session, and no explicit size cap on the SDP payload. create_offer holds session_lock while waiting up to 15 seconds for ICE gathering, so one request stalls every other offer. The only control is a README sentence telling operators not to expose it, while the same repository ships a full requirements.txt that makes running the demo easy.
security_findings.evidence: app/main.py:65 declares `@app.post('/api/webrtc/offer')` with no auth dependency; app/main.py:152-183 calls vision.analyze with the server-side GEMINI_API_KEY; app/main.py:144-203 returns the active session image, audio and ZIP; app/main.py:75-82 holds session_lock across setRemoteDescription and up to 15 seconds of ICE gathering; README.md:16 only warns not to put app.main:app on the Internet.
security_findings.impact: If bound to 0.0.0.0 or tunnelled like the mobile API already is, any stranger can burn the operator paid Gemini quota, read the active user photo, audio, transcript and export bundle, and exhaust CPU or file descriptors with unthrottled offers.
security_findings.recommendation: Remove the demo from the deployable image and public requirements, or add Bearer authentication, loopback binding at the socket level, per-IP rate limiting and a body cap; separate demo dependencies from the mobile runtime.

security_findings.title: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 Zipformer weights are baked into the distributable container image
security_findings.description: The model stage downloads hynt/Zipformer-30M-RNNT-Streaming-6000h into /opt/zipformer and the runtime stage copies it in, so every built image redistributes the weights. README.md states the weights are CC BY-NC-ND 4.0; NC forbids commercial use, ND forbids distributing modified or derivative weights including quantisation and fine-tuning needed for latency work, and attribution terms are not packaged as a NOTICE.
security_findings.evidence: Dockerfile:7 runs `python scripts/download_model.py --model-dir /opt/zipformer`; Dockerfile:24 copies `/opt/zipformer` into the runtime image; model_config.json:2 pins `hynt/Zipformer-30M-RNNT-Streaming-6000h`; README.md:109 states CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 and README.md:112 warns not to relicense the weights.
security_findings.impact: A funded or paid pilot, or pushing the image to any registry, is a licence violation; model optimisation is foreclosed because a quantised or fine-tuned derivative cannot be distributed.
security_findings.recommendation: Keep weights out of the image and download or mount them at runtime under the operator own licence acceptance; package attribution and NOTICE material; evaluate a permissively licensed Vietnamese ASR model for any commercial path.

security_findings.title: Gemini client honours proxy environment variables and can send the API key through an unintended proxy
security_findings.description: GeminiVisionProvider builds an httpx.AsyncClient without trust_env=False, so httpx honours HTTPS_PROXY, ALL_PROXY, SSL_CERT_FILE and related environment variables. The Gemini API key is sent in the x-goog-api-key header. The research fetcher deliberately sets trust_env=False in two places, so the egress policy is inconsistent; a compromised or misconfigured proxy environment can route the key, image and transcript through an unintended intermediary.
security_findings.evidence: app/vision.py:221 creates `httpx.AsyncClient(timeout=self._timeout, transport=self._transport)` without trust_env=False; app/vision.py:224 sends `headers={'x-goog-api-key': self._api_key}`; app/guidance_search.py:159 and app/guidance_search.py:230 explicitly set trust_env=False.
security_findings.impact: A server-side environment compromise or platform misconfiguration can expose the Gemini key and user media to a proxy, and egress becomes non-deterministic across deployments.
security_findings.recommendation: Pass trust_env=False to the Gemini client, document the required egress path, and add a regression test with proxy environment variables set; consider a dedicated egress client or allowlist.

security_findings.title: Admission control is process-local and breaks when the service scales beyond one worker
security_findings.description: WorkGate is an in-memory dict of leases with capacity 2 and one identity per token. The Docker image runs uvicorn with --workers 1 and the Cloud Run reference uses --max-instances 1; the documentation itself notes that multiple replicas need shared admission. Any horizontal scale-out, or an accidental --workers 2, gives each process its own gate, so the documented one-active-per-token and two-global-AI-job limits no longer hold.
security_findings.evidence: app/mobile_security.py:79-88 stores leases in a local dict and checks `len(self._leases) >= self.capacity or identity in self._leases`; Dockerfile:30 runs `--workers 1`; docs/ANDROID_SETUP.md:88 says multiple replicas need shared admission.
security_findings.impact: Under scale-out one token can run multiple concurrent AI jobs, and the operator can exceed the intended Gemini concurrency and cost envelope; CPU and STT contention and quota exhaustion become possible.
security_findings.recommendation: Move admission to a shared atomic store such as Redis with a per-token lease and a global semaphore, or enforce a single instance and fail startup when workers exceed one; add a regression test with two app instances sharing one gate.

security_findings.title: Static bearer tokens have no expiry, rotation or per-token request quota
security_findings.description: Trial tokens are 256-bit random values, but the server stores only SHA-256 digests with no issued_at, expiry, label or usage counter. Revocation requires editing TRIAL_TOKEN_HASHES and restarting the process. There is no per-token request-rate or spend cap; the gate only limits concurrent jobs. A leaked token therefore remains valid indefinitely and can serially consume Gemini quota until an operator notices and restarts.
security_findings.evidence: app/mobile_security.py:19-27 stores only a tuple of 64-hex digests; app/mobile_security.py:37-46 hashes the presented token and compares; docs/ANDROID_SETUP.md:28-35 describes revocation by deleting the hash and restarting; app/mobile_security.py:76-88 limits concurrency rather than request rate.
security_findings.impact: Lost or stolen tester tokens grant indefinite access; there is no per-user audit trail or spend attribution; incident response requires a full process restart.
security_findings.recommendation: Store token metadata including label, issued_at, expires_at, last_used and request_count; enforce expiry and a per-token rate or spend budget; support revocation without restart through a Redis denylist; log a token identifier, never the token.

security_findings.title: Dependencies are version-pinned but not hash-locked and there is no CI vulnerability gate
security_findings.description: requirements.txt and requirements-mobile.txt pin versions but contain no require-hashes directives; the Docker base images are pinned by tag rather than digest; there is no GitHub Actions workflow, pip-audit, npm audit, osv-scanner, Dependabot, Renovate or SBOM generation. scripts/check.sh only runs tests, compileall, a JavaScript syntax check and TypeScript and Jest. A mutable dependency or base-image tag can enter the build without an automated CVE or provenance gate.
security_findings.evidence: requirements.txt:1-56 lists exact versions but no hashes; Dockerfile:1 and Dockerfile:10 use tag-only base images; scripts/check.sh:5-10 runs pytest, compileall, node --check, typecheck and Jest only; the only YAML workflow found is mobile/.eas/workflows/repack-android.yml.
security_findings.impact: A compromised or vulnerable dependency can ship unnoticed; builds are not bit-reproducible; there is no machine-readable SBOM for a safety-critical assistive product.
security_findings.recommendation: Use a lockfile with hashes via uv or pip-tools, pin image digests, add CI with pip-audit, npm audit and osv-scanner plus an SBOM such as CycloneDX or Syft, and enable automated dependency updates.

security_findings.title: Admin localhost check is address-based and can be bypassed by a local reverse proxy or tunnel
security_findings.description: The admin app allows requests only when the Host header hostname is 127.0.0.1, localhost or ::1 and request.client.host is loopback or testclient. This is correct for direct localhost use, but it cannot distinguish a local browser from a reverse proxy or tunnel that terminates on loopback and forwards a remote request with a spoofed Host header. The documentation explicitly forbids tunnelling the admin port, but a single operator mistake would expose the admin surface.
security_findings.evidence: app/guidance_admin.py:82 checks `if hostname not in {'127.0.0.1','localhost','::1'} or client not in {'127.0.0.1','::1','testclient'}`; docs/GUIDANCE_040.md:45 says not to forward the admin page, PostgreSQL or Redis.
security_findings.impact: Misconfiguration could expose the knowledge-approval UI; the login secret and CSRF and session controls still apply, but the attack surface and credential-phishing risk increase.
security_findings.recommendation: Bind the admin listener to loopback at the socket level or use a Unix socket, reject forwarded headers, and add a deployment check that the admin port is unreachable through the mobile tunnel.

# Technical Review Report: APEC Mắt Kính Cho Người Khiếm Thị

**Reviewed target:** `target/APEC_mat_kinh_cho_nguoi_khiem_thi` at commit `d9ba1e0d42e1241471b1fb58df1efb9d345c6721` (2026-10-28).
**Review date:** 2026-10-31.
**Reviewer:** DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017.
**Boundary:** This report assesses only the external codebase in `target/`. The `review1` harness was not reviewed. No target files were modified.

---

## 1. Executive Summary and Readiness Verdict

The target is **Mắt Kính**, an Android assistive application for blind and low-vision Vietnamese users. The shipped product is not a pair of smart glasses; it is a phone application that captures a rear-camera still image, accepts a spoken question, sends a bounded JPEG and M4A clip over HTTPS to an operator-run FastAPI service, transcribes the audio with a server-side Zipformer model, asks Google Gemini about the image plus transcript, and speaks the Vietnamese answer through the device TTS engine or TalkBack. A newer v3 flow adds a stateful remote-control guidance loop that can ask for additional photos, demand model-label evidence, and verify a target-device screen before declaring a step complete.

The engineering is genuinely stronger than the typical pilot. Authentication is fail-closed, only token digests are stored, request bodies are capped before multipart parsing, concurrency is bounded by a per-token and global admission gate, audio is never sent to Gemini, media is not persisted as history, and the v3 orchestrator treats model output as an untrusted proposal rather than an instruction. The accessibility work is also real: touch targets are large, text scales, the camera preview is hidden from the accessibility tree, and the native volume-key policy explicitly yields to TalkBack gestures and Android system shortcuts.

The project is nevertheless **not production-ready** and should be treated as a **supervised field pilot only**:

- There is **no LICENSE** in a repository that is publicly readable, while the README claims the opposite. The CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 Zipformer weights are baked into the container image.
- There is **no CI**, no Python linter or type checker, no coverage threshold, no dependency hashing and no SBOM. The only release tag, `v0.1.0`, points at the 0.4 implementation commit.
- **No real device or blind user has completed the acceptance checklist.** Every row in the guidance and Android acceptance tables is still `Chưa thử` (not tested).
- A **legacy WebRTC demo** remains in the same repository with no authentication and access to the server's paid Gemini key. It is documented as local-only, but it is one operator mistake away from exposure.
- The **front door is inconsistent**: it mixes a macOS Chrome demo, an unintegrated LiDAR sensor, a stale model default and temporary tunnel URLs.

### Scorecard

| Dimension | Score | Rationale |
|---|---:|---|
| Overall | **7.8** | Strong safety and privacy engineering, weak release engineering and zero user validation. |
| Architecture | **8.6** | Clear client/server split, explicit v2 and v3 boundaries, layered security and guidance modules. Two server entry points and two client state machines add debt. |
| Code quality | **8.2** | Strict TypeScript, typed Python, small focused modules and strong validation; but no Python static analysis, no linting, dead v2 client path, broad exception boundaries and some large orchestrator functions. |
| Security | **8.0** | Excellent auth, input, SSRF and prompt-injection controls; legacy demo, static token lifecycle, proxy-env egress, process-local admission and licensing gaps pull the score down. |
| Documentation | **6.4** | Extensive Vietnamese docs and acceptance checklists, undermined by a misleading front door, stale links, model-version drift, a mispointed tag and no licence. |

### Readiness tiers

| Tier | Verdict |
|---|---|
| Local developer demo | Ready, with the explicit caveat that `app.main:app` must never be exposed. |
| Supervised pilot with known testers | Conditional. Technically credible, but only after the licence, legacy demo and real-device checklist are resolved. |
| Unsupervised use by blind users | Not ready. No real-user validation, no production identity lifecycle, no device matrix, and no continuous monitoring. |
| Commercial deployment | Blocked by the CC BY-NC-ND weights and the absent repository licence. |

---

## 2. Project Identity, Purpose and Hardware Reality Check

### 2.1 Problem domain and audience

The application addresses a real accessibility problem: a blind or low-vision user wants to ask about what is in front of them, read a label, locate an object, or receive step-by-step help operating a TV or air-conditioner remote. The interface is deliberately voice-first and hardware-key-friendly because touch-screen exploration is slow and error-prone for the target user.

The domain vocabulary is Vietnamese: `Bắt đầu nói`, `Chụp và gửi`, `Đã làm`, `Chưa tìm thấy`, `Nghe lại bước này`, `Đổi mục tiêu`, `Hủy hướng dẫn`. The documentation, error messages, tests and prompts are consistently in Vietnamese, which is appropriate for the intended pilot audience.

### 2.2 What the repository actually ships

There are three operational surfaces:

1. **`app.mobile_api:app`** — the production mobile API (v2 analysis and transcription, v3 guidance routes). Documented as the only backend that may be public (`README.md:16`).
2. **`app.main:app`** — a legacy local WebRTC demo with a browser UI under `web/`. It captures one photo and one audio clip, transcribes locally, optionally calls Gemini, and can export a ZIP. It is explicitly local-only.
3. **`app.guidance_admin:app`** — a localhost-only knowledge-approval UI for device manuals, separate from the mobile API.

The Android application lives in `mobile/` and is built with Expo SDK 57 and React Native 0.86.3. The APK is built through EAS, not through the Python Docker image.

### 2.3 Hardware reality vs aspirational claims

The repository name and README use **Mắt Kính** (glasses), but the operational product is a **phone app**. There is no glasses hardware, no head-mounted display, no camera bridge and no wearable integration in the codebase.

The README has a section titled **LIDAR sensor ST Electronics VL53L9CX** with a marketing image and a note that software has to analyse it (`README.md:118-124`). A repository-wide search finds `VL53`, `LiDAR` and `ToF` only in `README.md:118-124`; there is no driver, parser, distance pipeline, calibration file or test. The sensor is aspirational, not integrated.

The hardware-control feature is real but limited: the Kotlin Expo module intercepts short volume-up and volume-down presses while the assistant screen is in the foreground. It deliberately does **not** create an accessibility service, foreground service or media session. The docs describe headset/BLE integration as a future step and confirm that no BLE or media-session adapter exists (`docs/HARDWARE_CONTROLS_030.md:37-43`; `docs/IMPLEMENTATION_STATUS.md:64`). The `ControlSource` type includes `headset` (`mobile/src/core/controlInput.ts:2`), but there is no production adapter that emits it.

**Verdict:** the product identity should be described as an Android assistive app with optional phone volume-key control, not as smart glasses or a LiDAR wearable.

### 2.4 Maintenance status and maturity

The target has five commits between 2026-09-28 and 2026-10-28, from two contributors:

| Metric | Value |
|---|---|
| Commits | 5 |
| Contributors | 2 (`Matthias Kreier`, `thanh1912-ut`) |
| Branches | `main`, `ToF`, `ver1` |
| Tags | `v0.1.0` only |
| Tag target | `16faf3f` — the commit titled *Implement Mat Kinh 0.4 Android device guidance* |
| Tracked paths | 142 |
| Analyzer count | 138 files, 34 directories, 27,525 lines |

The single tag is mispointed: `v0.1.0` resolves to `16faf3f`, which is the 0.4 implementation commit, not the 0.1.0 release. The documented 0.1.0 through 0.4.0 releases therefore cannot be reconstructed from tags or a meaningful commit history. This is a release-integrity problem, not merely a documentation gap.
